counterfactual_missing_items: No evidence of arteriovenous malformations or capillary malformations to support CM-AVM
No limb overgrowth or port-wine stain to support Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome
No thrombocytopenia or other hematologic abnormality to support cutaneovisceral angiomatosis with thrombocytopenia
decisive_items: Detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant.
Family history revealed similar conditions in the patient's father and aunt, with the father having died of an intracranial hemorrhage in his early 70s.
The patient used a wheelchair due to right-sided hemiparesis and hemianopsia caused by an intracranial hemorrhage
response.rationale: C1 uniquely integrates the pathogenic KRIT1 variant with the autosomal dominant family history of intracranial hemorrhage, directly establishing familial cerebral cavernous malformations. R7 captures the genetic and neurological features but omits the familial context, making it a less complete but still strong alternative. Other candidates either misattribute the KRIT1 variant (R6) or rely on non-specific skin findings without genetic correlation (R2, R4, R5, R1).

rejected.why: Only cites sonographic slow-flow malformations, which are non-specific and not linked to the KRIT1 variant or family history.
Suggests cutaneovisceral angiomatosis with thrombocytopenia, but no thrombocytopenia or visceral involvement is present; histopathology is more consistent with cavernous malformations.
Associates KRIT1 with CM-AVM, but KRIT1 is specific to cerebral cavernous malformations, not CM-AVM (which is RASA1/EPHB4).
Lipolymphedema is a secondary finding, not a primary diagnosis, and lacks any genetic or histopathologic support.
Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome requires limb overgrowth and capillary malformations, which are absent; the KRIT1 variant is not associated with this syndrome.
